text:
Vegas is winless in four (0-1-3), and it's the most deceiving slump on tonight's board. The Golden Knights had 56% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) across those games and still got outscored 17-11. Three of the four went past regulation, the latest a shootout loss to Dallas. They remain at 96% to make the playoffs by our numbers. Still, the beat noticed Jack Eichel's frustration on a power play this week, and he has only three even-strength points in his last 12 games. Ivan Barbashev is back on the top line after a short experiment, per the coverage.

The bright spot is Victor Olofsson, who has 11 points (7 goals) in his last ten in his second stint in Vegas, and it's earned: his own chances are up and so is his ice time, by almost two minutes a night. Mitch Marner is one assist from 600 and has a ten-game home point streak, though tonight he's on the road. Carter Hart starts, at .888 this season. Noah Hanifin is off ESPN's injury report and could return.

Winnipeg comes in 4-1-0 in its last five, outscoring teams 22-14, with Josh Morrissey's first goal of the season ending Thursday's game against the Islanders in overtime. Mark Scheifele has been in 30 headlines in two weeks, a lot of them about his place in Jets history, and Kyle Connor is at 18 goals. The underlying numbers are softer than the record: 47% of the five-on-five expected goals and a 30% playoff chance. Stuart Skinner starts, at .883 with a goal saved above expected. Nino Niederreiter is a point from 500 for his career, Alex Iafallo a point from 300.

Our numbers lean Vegas, 3.38 expected goals to 3.04. Connor is at 46% to score, and Trevor Connelly is our Vegas sleeper at 23%.
headline: Vegas is losing games it's winning on paper
